cards.q: What is the difference between dead and imposed loads on a structure?
options: Dead loads move; imposed loads stay still
Dead: its own weight; imposed: what it carries
Imposed loads only ever come from wind
They are two names for the same load
cards.why: Designs combine them with safety factors (Eurocode 1 in the UK).

cards.q: Why does concrete have steel reinforcement?
options: Concrete is weak in tension; steel takes it
Steel makes the concrete set faster
To stop the concrete conducting electricity
To make the concrete lighter overall
cards.why: The bars go where the member is pulled: the bottom of a simply supported beam.

cards.q: A simply supported beam of span {l} m carries a uniform load of {w} kN/m. What is the largest bending moment, in kN·m?
cards.why: For a uniform load: $M_{max} = \frac{wL^2}{8}$, at mid-span.

cards.q: Two streams of {a} kg/h and {b} kg/h feed a mixer with one outlet and no build-up. What leaves, in kg/h?
cards.why: Mass balance: in = out + accumulation; with no accumulation, out equals in.

cards.q: {m} kg/s of water is heated by {dt} K (c = 4.18 kJ/kg·K). What heat duty is that, in kW?
cards.why: $Q = mc\Delta T$, with m the mass flow: kg/s × kJ/kg·K × K = kJ/s = kW.

cards.q: Match each unit operation with what it does.
pairs: Moves heat from one stream to another
cards.why: Process plants are built from these standard pieces.

cards.q: Why do aircraft use aluminium alloys, titanium and composites?
options: They are the cheapest metals
They are the easiest to weld
They conduct heat very well
High strength for their weight
cards.why: Every kilogram saved is fuel saved or payload gained.

cards.q: Who regulates civil aircraft airworthiness in the UK?
options: The Health and Safety Executive
The Ministry of Defence
The Civil Aviation Authority (CAA)
BSI
cards.why: Since 2021 the UK CAA, not EASA, oversees UK civil airworthiness.

cards.q: A wing of {s} m² flies at {v} m/s in air of density 1.225 kg/m³ with a lift coefficient of {cl}. What lift does it make, in kN?
cards.why: $L = \frac{1}{2}\rho v^2 S C_L$: lift grows with the square of speed.

cards.q: A battery is {v} V and {ah} Ah. How much energy does it store, in kWh?
cards.why: Energy = volts × amp-hours: Wh; ÷ 1000 for kWh.

cards.q: A {kwp} kWp solar array in the UK yields about 900 kWh per kWp a year. How much energy is that a year, in kWh?
cards.why: Peak rating × the site's specific yield. Much more in summer than winter.

cards.q: Why does grid frequency fall when demand exceeds generation?
options: Transformers overheat and lose efficiency
Generators slow as they give up stored energy
Cables stretch and get longer
The meters start to read wrongly
cards.why: Rotating machines' inertia covers the gap for a moment; frequency response then adds power. In GB the grid runs at 50 Hz, held within narrow limits.

cards.q: How many axes does a typical industrial arm have, to reach any position at any angle?
options: Six
Three
Two
Twelve
cards.why: Three to place the wrist, three to orient the tool.

cards.q: Why teach points in a user (work-object) frame rather than the robot's base frame?
options: User frames make the robot move faster
The base frame cannot store any points
It stops the robot colliding with things
Re-teach the frame and every point follows
cards.why: Points are relative to the fixture, so moving the fixture needs only its frame re-taught.

cards.q: A two-link planar arm has links of {l1} mm and {l2} mm. The first joint is at {t1}° and the second at {t2}° (relative to the first link). How far along x is the tip, in mm?
cards.why: Forward kinematics: $x = L_1\cos\theta_1 + L_2\cos(\theta_1 + \theta_2)$; the second link's angle adds to the first.
